data.title: Holland America Line's 2028-2029 Asia Cruise Season Blooms with Cherry Blossoms and Five New Ports
data.description:
Holland America Line's 2028-2029 Asia Cruise Season Blooms with Cherry Blossoms and Five New Ports

Holland America Line's 2028-2029 Asia Cruise Season Blooms with Cherry Blossoms and Five New Ports

PR Newswire

SEATTLE, Nov. 20, 2026

Eurodam's first Asia season features new destinations, more time ashore and opportunities to experience Japan during its famed cherry blossom season

Key Takeaways:

  • Eurodam makes its Asia debut with five new ports, expanding Holland America Line's 2028-2029 season across Japan, South Korea, China, Taiwan, the Philippines and Southeast Asia.
  • More time ashore and Japan's cherry blossom season deepen the destination experience, with overnight stays and late-night departures across 14 ports, plus spring sailings timed to give guests opportunities to see the famed blooms.
  • A new 27-day Coffee, Tea & Spice Route Legendary Voyage expands longer exploration of the region, visiting 13 ports across seven countries and bringing Asia's culinary traditions on board through destination-inspired experiences.

SEATTLE, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Holland America Line announced its 2028-2029 Asia cruise season, adding five new ports across Japan, Taiwan, Brunei and the Philippines to a wide-ranging collection of cruises throughout the region. Aboard Eurodam, making its Asia debut, cruises explore Japan, South Korea, China, Taiwan, the Philippines and Southeast Asia.

 Five new ports, more time ashore and Japan's cherry blossoms highlight Holland America Line's 2028-2029 Asia season.

Sailing from September 2028 through May 2029, the season features itineraries ranging from 11 to 27 days, with departures from Tokyo, Japan; Hong Kong, China; and Singapore. Standout cruises range from in-depth explorations of Japan to journeys connecting the major cities and islands of Southeast Asia, with 14 overnight ports adding extra time ashore.

"Asia is one of those regions where you can experience something completely different from one port to the next, from a major city like Hong Kong to our new call at Coron in the Philippines, known for its turquoise waters and rich history," said Paul Grigsby, vice president of deployment and revenue planning for Holland America Line. "That contrast is what makes these itineraries so interesting to build. The new ports take guests beyond the places they may already know, introducing them to islands, coastlines and historic communities that reveal another side of the region, while natural phenomena like Japan's cherry blossoms can make the experience completely different depending on when you visit."

The five new ports add a mix of tropical landscapes, natural wonders and historic sites to the season.

  • Coron, Busuanga Island, Philippines, is known for the emerald Twin Lagoons.
  • Japan offers two new locales: Hirara introduces guests to the white-sand beaches and turquoise waters of Miyako Island, while Wakayama offers access to Wakayama Castle and the sacred mountain temples of Koyasan.
  • Magong showcases the striking basalt coastline of Taiwan's Penghu Island.
  • Muara provides a gateway to Brunei Darussalam and the gold-domed Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque.

Spring brings another reason to explore Japan as the country's famed cherry blossom season unfolds across different regions. Guests sailing spring itineraries can seek out the blooms along their journey, while those embarking in Tokyo can extend their stay before or after their cruise for more time to experience the season ashore. Shore excursions provide additional opportunities to take in the seasonal color, including from Kobe, where guests can visit UNESCO World Heritage-listed Himeji Castle and neighboring Koko-en Garden, known for its cherry blossoms in early spring.

More Time to Explore
Across the 2028-2029 Asia season, guests can enjoy overnight stays and late-night departures in 14 ports throughout the region. The additional time ashore creates a more relaxed pace, with opportunities to experience a city after dark, linger over dinner, revisit a favorite spot or take part in longer excursions. By extending time in port into the evening or the following day, guests can experience more of a destination's local culture, cuisine and nightlife without feeling rushed.

  • Overnight ports throughout Asia include Bali, Indonesia; Halong Bay, Vietnam; Hong Kong, China; Incheon (Seoul), South Korea; Keelung (Taipei), Taiwan; Laem Chabang (Bangkok), Thailand; Manila, Philippines; Hiroshima, Osaka and Maizuru, Japan; Phú Mỹ (Ho Chi Minh City) and Halong Bay, Vietnam; Shanghai, China; and Singapore. New overnight stays for the 2028-2029 season include Keelung and Phú Mỹ.
  • Guests can take advantage of extended stays by watching a sunset in Halong Bay, exploring Manila's historic San Agustin Church or experiencing Shanghai's neon city lights after dark.
  • Late-night departures also give guests additional time in Fukuoka, Hiroshima, Maizuru and Osaka, Japan; Halong Bay, Vietnam; and Shanghai, China.

Coffee, Tea and Spice Take Center Stage on New 27-Day Legendary Voyage
New for 2029, Holland America Line will introduce a 27-day Coffee, Tea & Spice Route Legendary Voyage aboard Eurodam, departing Jan. 3 roundtrip from Singapore. The itinerary visits 13 ports across seven countries, tracing the region's coffee, tea and spice traditions from Java and Manila to Taiwan and Hong Kong, with overnight calls in Bali, Hong Kong and  Phú Mỹ, the gateway to Ho Chi Minh City. On board, Holland America Line plans to bring the journey to life through regionally inspired tea and coffee experiences.

2028-2029 Asia Season Highlights

  • Circle Japan: 11- and 14-day itineraries sail roundtrip or between Tokyo and Yokohama (Tokyo), exploring ports throughout Japan and South Korea. The 14-day cruises visit up to 10 ports, with select extended calls in Hiroshima; the 11-day April 22, 2029, cruise features an overnight in Maizuru.
  • Japan & South Korea Discovery: Two 14-day cruises explore Japan and South Korea, with an overnight in Incheon (Seoul) and extended calls in Osaka and/or Fukuoka. The 11-day Southern Japan & Jeju Discovery, departing May 3, 2029, adds a call at Jeju.
  • Japan, Taiwan & China: The 14-day Japan & Taiwan cruise departs Nov. 5, 2028, from Tokyo to Hong Kong, with overnights in Osaka and Keelung (Taipei). A 14-day China & Japan Discovery departing Feb. 25, 2029, features overnights in Shanghai and Osaka.
  • Southeast Asia Discovery: The 14-day Nov. 19, 2028, sailing from Hong Kong to Singapore features overnights in Laem Chabang (Bangkok) and Halong Bay. A 17-day holiday itinerary departs Dec. 17, adding Nha Trang, Vietnam, and Kota Kinabalu, Malaysia, along with festive onboard programming.
  • Thailand & Philippines Discovery: The 14-day Dec. 3 sailing from Singapore to Hong Kong features six ports, including overnights in Laem Chabang (Bangkok) and Manila.
  • North Pacific Crossings: Two cruises connect Asia with the Pacific Northwest: a 13-day Vancouver-to-Tokyo crossing with Ketchikan, Alaska, and scenic cruising through the Inside Passage, and a 14-day Tokyo-to-Seattle crossing featuring Kushiro, Japan, and three Alaska ports.

Guests looking to spend even longer in the region can combine select back-to-back itineraries into Collectors' Voyages, extending their exploration across multiple countries and destinations.

Bringing Asia's Flavors On Board
Holland America Line's Destination Dining program brings the itinerary onboard, with menus inspired by the places guests visit. For the 2028-2029 Asia season, guests can sample flavors from throughout the region with dishes including Japanese rockfish and fresh sushi, Korean bibimbap with beef bulgogi, Thai mango sticky rice, Filipino chicken adobo, matcha lava cake, Indonesian coconut-filled pancakes and Vietnamese-style fresh spring rolls.

Have It All Early Booking Bonus
For a limited time, when guests book 2028-2029 Asia cruises with the Have It All premium package, the standard package amenities of shore excursions, specialty dining, a Signature Beverage Package and Surf Wi-Fi are included — plus the added perk of free prepaid crew appreciation, along with free upgrades to the Elite Beverage Package and Premium Wi-Fi. 

Guests can also take advantage of Holland America Line's Exclusive Mariner Society Early Booking Bonus. Mariner Society loyalty members can enjoy up to $400 onboard credit per stateroom. 

For more information about Holland America Line or to book a cruise, consult a travel advisor, call 1-877-SAIL HAL (877-724-5425) or visit hollandamerica.com. 

Find Holland America Line on Facebook, Instagram and the Holland America Blog. You can also access all social media outlets via the home page at hollandamerica.com.

About Holland America Line
Holland America Line has been exploring the world for more than 150 years with expertly crafted itineraries, extraordinary service and genuine connections to the destinations. Offering a perfectly-sized ship experience, its fleet of 11 vessels visits nearly 400 ports in 114 countries around the world and has shared the thrill of Alaska for more than 75 years — longer than any other cruise line. Savour the Journey isn't just a tagline, it's a reinforcement that the cruise line provides experiences too good to hurry through, connecting travelers to the world and each other. Award-winning enrichment programming, entertainment and cuisine that brings each locale on board, including a revolutionary Global Fresh Fish Program, put Holland America Line at the forefront of premium cruising. Holland America Line is part of Carnival Corporation, the world's largest cruise company with a portfolio of cruise lines operating in over 800 ports & destinations worldwide. (NYSE: CCL).

data.title: My husband spent $80,000 on a boat, yet says my plans for a $100,000 pottery studio are irresponsible. Who's right?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'We have $2.9 million in retirement accounts and a paid-off house worth $900,000'

"My husband says that's too much to risk on something that may never turn a profit." (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

I'm 62, my husband is 65, and we've been married 31 years. We have $2.9 million in retirement accounts, a paid-off house worth $900,000, depending on the market, and very little debt. He retired last year. I now work part-time at a dental office, three days a week.

For 15 years I've wanted to open a small pottery studio. I've taken classes, sold mugs and planters at the Saturday market, and right now I throw on a wheel in our cold garage and pack everything away when I'm done.

There's a space near the old rail depot, about 900 square feet with a big front window, that would be perfect. Between the build-out, a kiln, wheels, insurance and a year of rent, I figure I'd need about $100,000.

My husband says that's too much to risk on something that may never turn a profit. He's afraid I'll keep pouring money into it if it struggles. He also brings up healthcare, inflation and one of us living to 95.

Three years ago he bought a boat for $80,000, then spent another $12,000 on a new motor and a fish finder. He barely used it after the first summer and finally sold it at a loss. He says that's different because he never claimed the boat would make money.

I'm not claiming the studio will make us rich either. I'd be happy if it paid for itself. I'm willing to write a real business plan, set a budget and agree on a number we're willing to lose. I'd even start smaller, though this space really is right. I haven't signed anything or spent a cent.

He says I'm proposing another job instead of retirement. To me, the work I choose is exactly what retirement should be. Am I being unrealistic about what $100,000 means for us? And how do two people decide what's a reasonable thing to spend on?

A 62-Year-Old Wife

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: 'I like the idea of a big return': My financial adviser wants me to invest $350,000 in a UAE data center. Is this risky?

Tell your husband that you're not giving up before you've even started.

Dear Wife,

From your letter, it doesn't sound like pottery is just a business for you.

For you, pottery is a passion, and it's important to have something you like doing in retirement. If you are going to choose to open a business, it should be something you will love because it won't always be easy, and you may need to rely on that bedrock of belief when the going gets tough. That's in addition to financial projections, advice from an accountant, knowing where you draw a hard line on the budget if sales dry up, and even a Plan B for the space.

I'm not going to tell you to open a business and spend $100,000, which could be a little on the high side, although you will know more when you compare this plan to similar-sized businesses and complete your due diligence. More important, I'm not going to tell you not to do it, and I don't think anyone else should, either, at least not without hearing you out, visiting the proposed site and, crucially, seeing your business plan. What stands out from your letter is your husband's immediate, possibly knee-jerk, opposition.

However, pointing out that he bought an $80,000 motorboat and ended up throwing good money after bad and selling it at a loss may be fair, but it doesn't help your cause. Yes, he decided to pursue something that he eventually tired of or decided wasn't worth all the hassle and expense. He's the one who apparently lost interest in a project after spending nearly six figures, not you. But it won't help to trade successes and failures in a tit-for-tat argument.

If a pottery studio is a vocation, you have earned the right to at least look into it.

It may be that you don't have to lease this building, as romantic as it sounds. You could rent a space at a retirement center or local school, at least initially, invest in the equipment to host pottery classes, build up word of mouth or an online presence and see how much demand is out there. That way, you won't be locked into a lease if the demand is not there. It will also help you envision what success means to you. Is it teaching a twice-weekly class? Or running a full-time studio?

You raise a great point when you say your retirement is not about doing nothing, or spending all of your time on the golf course or tennis court, or sitting in your garden reading - rather, it's about pursuing work that fulfills you. If pottery is a vocation for you, you have earned the right to at least look into it, given that you have worked for probably 40-plus years in jobs that helped you and your husband build a $2.9 million nest egg, even if those jobs were not your first choice.

For what it's worth, your business plan should include projected costs, including the lease, insurance, equipment, advertising, branding and marketing; projected revenue; the target market (there may be schools or senior centers nearby that would jump at the opportunity for their community to learn pottery); and, of course, the competition (find out if there are similar businesses in your area and, if so, how close they are and what they charge for classes).

Related: 'I don't want to die on the sales floor': I'm 67 and earn $19.50 an hour at a big-box store. When can I finally retire?

Running the numbers

You won't win this argument on statements that your husband is the proverbial pot calling the kettle black, and you may not "win" the argument at all. But you will lend more credence to your pottery studio idea through data. You have $2.9 million for retirement, a mortgage-free house worth $900,000, hardly any debt, a husband who has already retired, Social Security coming down the pike, and you continue to work part-time, although that may have to end if you set up this studio.

To put your small business in context: Startup costs of $100,000 represent 3.45% of your retirement account balance. That's not nothing, but neither is it an outrageous, extravagant risk, particularly given that this is an investment to further a pastime that brings you joy and, hopefully, makes money. What is your annual income now? What will it be in five years? What are your annual expenses? How much of your retirement is in traditional accounts versus Roth?

Another missing piece of this puzzle: Do you have a "fun money" account, an emergency fund or CDs or bonds to draw from? Otherwise, you would have to take this money from your investments. That would mean you need to take more than $100,000, because you would have to pay tax on the money you withdraw from a traditional IRA or 401(k). You would lose future investment returns (which you would ideally recoup, even if only in part, from your studio).

A $100,000 startup cost represents 3.45% of your retirement-account balance.

Tell your husband that you're not giving up before you've even started, just as you would not expect him to give up on a passion project without at least stress-testing the finances. The unspoken part of this conversation, particularly after his motorboat project, is hanging over you. It does not sound like you are asking him for permission, per se - rather, you are requesting his support, and I assume you have both contributed to your retirement fund, either as a corporate worker or a homemaker.

Agree on a maximum amount you can afford to lose on a studio. You will need working capital, particularly in the early stages, when you are building your reputation. This is an opportunity to step back and ask what you want from retirement. How do you want to spend your savings? What kind of issues require unanimous agreement? (Did you agree to the motorboat purchase, for instance?) How will you navigate such issues while respecting each other's space?

A woman named Kyla Glendenning opened up a pottery studio in Fort Lauderdale and said she had revenue of $71,000 in the first six months, but spent nearly $20,000 on Facebook advertisements. That tells me, in addition to the costs of setting up a studio, signing a lease and buying equipment, that your biggest challenges will be getting the word out that you exist. Her online tutorials and videos on social media - where I found her - also require both time and money.

Don't let anyone crack your bowls before they've even hit the kiln.

Related: My wife says we can't afford to retire. I vetoed her $8,000 trip to Italy. We're in our 60s and have $4 million. Do I keep working?

data.title: Here's what happened next after previous times the S&P 500 losing streak reached six sessions
data.description:
By Steve Goldstein

Six-session losing runs are relatively rare, but they're not necessarily a bad sign of future returns.

For markets, it's been a week from hell - or, more accurately, the worst stretch for the S&P 500 since the "Liberation Day" tariffs of 2025 - but the history of six-session losing streaks actually points to some better news ahead.

First, inspired by a message from the OddStats social-media account, MarketWatch looked at the last nine times the S&P 500 had a six-day losing streak like this one where it's lost at least 5%.

The S&P 500 SPX was positive the next day, seven out of nine times, with a median return of 1.9%. (OddStats said it was up eight out of nine times; there may be confusion owing to the fact that one of the days occurred around the Thanksgiving holiday.)

The early action in S&P 500 futures (ES00) on Friday doesn't look great for this particular streak, however things can of course change; that same contract was higher in the premarket on Thursday before closing much lower.

Next comes this nugget from Ben Kizemchuk, a portfolio manager at Wellington-Altus, who looked more longer term.

He noted there have been just 57 occasions where the S&P 500 closed lower for six straight sessions since 1975.

The average path afterward was positive across every forward time horizon studied, with gains improving from +0.6% after one week to +2.6% after roughly six weeks. The index was higher 68%-70% of the time after 10-25 trading days.

MarketWatch crunched the numbers. 

 
Horizon                  Sample Size  Mean Return (%)  Median Return (%)  Win Rate (%) 
Next_Day (1d)            57           0.42             0.34               64.9 
1_Week (5d)              57           0.6              0.7                66.7 
2_Weeks (10d)            57           0.56             0.68               57.9 
3_Weeks (15d)            57           1.02             1.51               68.4 
4_Weeks (20d)            57           2.28             2.16               68.4 
5_Weeks (25d)            57           2.36             2.19               70.2 
6_Weeks (30d)            57           2.65             1.23               66.7 
Source: Yfinance/Gemini

"While not a timing signal, the historical evidence suggests persistent selling pressure tends to be associated with seller exhaustion more often than the start of larger declines," said Kizemchuk.

-Steve Goldstein

data.title: VIGGO Launches Mix1Pro Commercial Cleaning Robot at ISSA Show North America 2026
data.description:
VIGGO Launches Mix1Pro Commercial Cleaning Robot at ISSA Show North America 2026

VIGGO Launches Mix1Pro Commercial Cleaning Robot at ISSA Show North America 2026

PR Newswire

LAS VEGAS, Nov. 20, 2026

Full product lineup addresses cleaning needs across indoor facilities, parking garages and outdoor spaces.

LAS VEGAS, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- VIGGO, a leading provider of commercial cleaning robots, showcased its full product lineup at ISSA Show North America 2026 (November 17–19), introducing its new Mix1Pro commercial cleaning robot to the global market.

The launch comes as commercial cleaning robots expand into more public spaces. According to IDC, global shipments reached approximately 58,000 units in 2025, an increase of 83.8% year over year. Building services, retail, transportation, hospitality and food service together accounted for 72.9% of shipments. For facility operators, long-term adoption depends on both cleaning performance and a robot's ability to adapt to changing conditions and work effectively alongside staff. Mix1Pro addresses these requirements through advances in navigation, cleaning and automated servicing.

Adaptive Navigation for Complex Environments

Mix1Pro combines 3D LiDAR with multi-sensor fusion to deliver 360-degree spatial perception. By detecting surrounding structures and tracking changes in its environment, the robot supports stable localization and responsive obstacle avoidance in complex, dynamic spaces.

Versatile Floor Care in One Machine

Mix1Pro sweeps, scrubs, vacuums and mops simultaneously in a single pass. Capable of both hard-floor care and carpet vacuuming, it accommodates diverse surfaces within a single facility. A 20.5-inch cleaning width supports efficient coverage, while an optional UV-C module adds disinfection capability.

Automated Servicing and Simpler Maintenance

Mix1Pro's fully automated docking station handles charging, clean-water refilling, wastewater draining, detergent dosing and self-cleaning of the scrubbing roller and roller brush. These functions reduce routine manual intervention and support extended autonomous operation.

A quick-release design simplifies daily maintenance, while an integrated ergonomic power-assisted handle and a 10-inch touchscreen make manual relocation and on-device operation more convenient.

Designed for shopping centers, supermarkets, hospitals, schools, hotels and office buildings, Mix1Pro accommodates varied floor types and cleaning requirements. Its quiet, efficient operation helps facilities maintain cleanliness alongside daily business activities and public services.

A Broader Portfolio for Specialized Cleaning Needs

Also on display were VIGGO's established product lines for other commercial environments.

The newly upgraded SC50ProPlus features hardware and software enhancements tailored to parking garages. Building on the SC50 series' versatility across indoor environments, these upgrades further strengthen its ability to sustain cleaning operations in these demanding settings.

The SC80 series draws on extensive deployment experience in industrial and logistics facilities across multiple international markets. Its long runtime and deep-cleaning capabilities address the demands of large areas and intensive cleaning schedules.

Designed for outdoor areas within enclosed or controlled-access sites, the S100-N is already operating across the Middle East, Europe and Asia. It provides autonomous sweeping for plazas, parks and roads within managed properties.

Practical Value for Facility Operators

VIGGO's commercial cleaning robot portfolio spans indoor and outdoor applications, with deployments in approximately 40 countries and regions. Sustained use across industrial facilities, transportation hubs and commercial properties has provided experience with a wide range of operating conditions.

From routine floor care to demanding cleaning tasks, the portfolio helps operators reduce manual workloads, simplify upkeep and maintain more consistent cleaning performance. By assigning repetitive cleaning work to robots, facilities can direct staff toward higher-value services and tasks requiring human judgment—improving both the quality of their spaces and the efficiency of their operations.

data.title: Nasdaq Set for Fresh Decline as AI Selloff Intensifies
data.description:
By Joe Stonor

Global stocks sold off and Treasurys strengthened as investor confidence in the artificial-intelligence trade showed signs of cracking.

Nasdaq futures dropped 1.15%, extending sharp falls from the last session. S&P 500 futures fell 0.5%, while contracts tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.1%. Major U.S. indexes are on track for their worst week since the announcement of President Trump's Liberation Day tariffs upended global trade in April 2025.

Anthropic's record-breaking IPO failed to stem heavy selling across global stocks. Chip makers, tech giants and cloud-computing stocks weakened in U.S. premarket trade after heavy selling across Asian tech names. The memory chip-dominated Kospi closed 5.2% lower, while Japan's Nikkei also fell more than 5%. Taiwan's Taiex sank 6.2%, bringing its weekly loss to more than 17%--its worst week since 1990.

The selling bled to European stocks, too. ASML, the continent's most valuable stock, fell more than 5% as a basket of the continent's tech stocks opened 3% lower. The continent-wide Stoxx 600 was 1.2% lower.

Demand for Anthropic's IPO is focusing attention on the sustainability of the AI investment buildout while also draining liquidity from the broader market, said Roger Lee, head of equity strategy at Cavendish.

The gloominess in stock market sentiment comes despite fresh declines for oil. Benchmark Brent crude contracts dropped around 1.25% to $90.85 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate contracts fell 1.7% to trade around $81.80 a barrel. The U.S. Energy Information Administration said Thursday that oil shipments through major Middle Eastern shipping routes increased 19% in the third quarter.

Lower oil prices and an investor flight to safety combined to strengthen Treasurys. Ten-year yields fell back below 5.000%, while two-year yields dropped 6 basis points to 4.720%. Thirty-year yields fell 3.1 basis points to trade around 5.370%.

Metals prices continued to sell off, with gold tumbling close to 3% at $3,580 a troy ounce. The dollar held near multimonth highs, while bitcoin rebounded slightly but remained near July lows, hovering just below $62,000.

For the day ahead, macro watchers will look to Michigan's consumer sentiment index for November, and to Federal Reserve speakers including Christopher Waller.

data.title: RLX Technology Announces Unaudited Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results
data.description:
RLX Technology Announces Unaudited Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

RLX Technology Announces Unaudited Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

PR Newswire

SHENZHEN, China, Nov. 20, 2026

SHENZHEN, China, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- RLX Technology Inc. ("RLX Technology" or the "Company") (NYSE: RLX), a leading global branded e-vapor company, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights

  • Net revenues were RMB1,916.6 million (US$285.9 million) in the third quarter of 2026, increasing by 69.7% from RMB1,129.3 million in the same period of 2025.
  • Gross profit increased by 26.7% to RMB446.6 million (US$66.6 million) in the third quarter of 2026.
  • Gross margin was 23.3% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 31.2% in the same period of 2025, primarily due to a change in the revenue mix following the consolidation of the Company's newly acquired European entity.
  • Non-GAAP income from operations[1] was RMB143.8 million (US$21.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB187.8 million in the same period of 2025.
  • U.S. GAAP net income was RMB147.1 million (US$21.9 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB206.8 million in the same period of 2025.
  • Non-GAAP net income[1] was RMB235.6 million (US$35.1 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB295.4 million in the same period of 2025.

"The third quarter marked a defining inflection point for RLX as we integrated our newly acquired European distribution platform with our existing retail footprint, evolving into a leading global smoke-free brand," said Ms. Ying (Kate) Wang, Co-founder, Chairperson, and Chief Executive Officer of RLX Technology. "We now possess end-to-end capabilities spanning global product innovation, supply chain execution, and direct route-to-market reach, while always placing our brands at the heart of adult consumers' choices worldwide. By pairing these strengths with dedicated local field teams and an open, multi-brand ecosystem philosophy, we are gaining sharper retail insights that will empower us to tailor products to local consumer preferences, scale our multi-category portfolio, and capture market share as shifting global regulations reshape the industry."

Mr. Chao Lu, Chief Financial Officer of RLX Technology, commented, "We delivered strong third quarter financial results, with the consolidation driving a surge in net revenues to RMB1.92 billion, up 69.7% year over year. International markets contributed 86.5% of our top line. While our blended gross margin now reflects the consolidation of the distribution business, we maintained solid non-GAAP profitability, improved working capital efficiency, and achieved a healthy sequential rebound in operating cash flow. Looking ahead, we are actively lifting our European platform's margins through supply chain optimization and capital deployment, while navigating transitional working capital needs related to the UK's October introduction of an excise duty. Supported by RMB13.48 billion in total financial assets, we have the financial flexibility to fund global brand expansion, deliver long-term sustainable growth, and maintain strong shareholder returns."

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Net revenues were RMB1,916.6 million (US$285.9 million) in the third quarter of 2026, increasing by 69.7% from RMB1,129.3 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily due to the consolidation of the Company's newly acquired European entity in July 2026. Net revenues from international business represented 86.5% of net revenues for the period.

Gross profit was RMB446.6 million (US$66.6 million) in the third quarter of 2026, increasing by 26.7% from RMB352.6 million in the same period of 2025.

Gross margin was 23.3% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with 31.2% in the same period of 2025, primarily due to a change in the revenue mix following the consolidation of the Company's newly acquired European entity.

Operating expenses were RMB407.1 million (US$60.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB259.3 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily due to higher salary and welfare expenses and increased shipping and logistics costs.

Selling expenses were RMB182.9 million (US$27.3 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB132.3 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to increases in salary and welfare expenses and shipping and logistics costs.

General and administrative expenses were RMB185.9 million (US$27.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB85.7 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to higher salary and welfare expenses and legal and other consulting fees.

Research and development expenses were RMB38.3 million (US$5.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB41.3 million in the same period of 2025.

U.S. GAAP income from operations was RMB39.5 million (US$5.9 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB93.3 million in the same period of 2025.

Non-GAAP income from operations was RMB143.8 million (US$21.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB187.8 million in the same period of 2025.

Income tax expense was RMB43.6 million (US$6.5 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB45.9 million in the same period of 2025.

U.S. GAAP net income was RMB147.1 million (US$21.9 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB206.8 million in the same period of 2025.

Non-GAAP net income was RMB235.6 million (US$35.1 million) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB295.4 million in the same period of 2025.

U.S. GAAP basic and diluted net income per American depositary share ("ADS") were RMB0.131 (US$0.020) and RMB0.123 (US$0.018), respectively, in the third quarter of 2026, compared with U.S. GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS of RMB0.167 and RMB0.157, respectively, in the same period of 2025.

Non-GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS[2] were RMB0.186 (US$0.028) and RMB0.175 (US$0.026), respectively, in the third quarter of 2026, compared with non-GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS of RMB0.236 and RMB0.221, respectively, in the same period of 2025.

[1] Non-GAAP net income and non-GAAP income from operations are non-GAAP financial measures. For more information on the Company's non-GAAP financial measures, please see the section "Non-GAAP Financial Measures" and the table captioned "Unaudited Reconciliation of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" set forth at the end of this press release.

[2] Non-GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS is a non-GAAP financial measure. For more information on the Company's non-GAAP financial measures, please see the section "Non-GAAP Financial Measures" and the table captioned "Unaudited Reconciliation of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" set forth at the end of this press release.

Balance Sheet and Cash Flow

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, short-term bank deposits, net, short-term investments, long-term bank deposits, net, and long-term investment securities, net, of RMB13,482.8 million (US$2,011.0 million), compared with RMB13,883.4 million as of June 30, 2026. In the third quarter of 2026, net cash generated from operating activities was RMB40.0 million (US$6.0 million).

Non-GAAP Financial Measures

The Company uses non-GAAP net income, non-GAAP income from operations and non-GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS, each a non-GAAP financial measure, in evaluating its operating results and for financial and operational decision-making purposes. Non-GAAP net income represents net income excluding share-based compensation expenses, amortization and depreciation of assets arising from fair value step-up in business acquisitions, and tax effects on non-GAAP adjustments. Non-GAAP income from operations represents net income from operations excluding share-based compensation expenses and amortization and depreciation of assets arising from fair value step-up in business acquisitions. Non-GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS is computed using non-GAAP net income attributable to RLX Technology Inc. and the same number of ADSs used in the U.S. GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS calculation.

The Company presents these non-GAAP financial measures because they are used by the management to evaluate its operating performance and formulate business plans. The Company believes that they help identify underlying trends in its business that could otherwise be distorted by the effect of certain expenses that are included in net income. The Company also believes that the use of the non-GAAP measures facilitates investors' assessment of its operating performance, as they could provide useful information about its operating results, enhance the overall understanding of its past performance and future prospects, and allow for greater visibility with respect to key metrics used by the management in its financial and operational decision making.

The non-GAAP financial measures are not defined under U.S. GAAP and are not presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. The non-GAAP financial measures have limitations as analytical tools.
